action_items: MINOR (non-blocking): In LinkedInSearch.jsx the React key on connection cards uses `key={conn.urn}` (line ~700) and on the Sending-to chips uses `key={c.urn}` (line ~750). Since urn is empty '' for all v5-synced connections, React logs 'Encountered two children with the same key' warnings (hundreds in console). Replace with `key={conn.public_id}` / `key={c.public_id}` to silence warnings and avoid future re-render/DOM-reconciliation edge cases.
critical_code_review_comments: React key collision: keys should use public_id everywhere in Messaging tab now that urn is empty. Functionality unaffected because selection state matches by public_id, but the warnings pollute console and could mask real bugs.

handleSendMessages only opens the FIRST selected connection's profile via window.open. For multi-select flows the user must click the quick-link chips manually for the other N-1. Consider clarifying UX copy or opening all sequentially with user confirmation.

rca of the issue: Bug 1 (Select All shows 1): toggleConnSelection previously matched by conn.urn; v5 browser sync script doesn't populate urn, so every connection had urn=='' which the .find(c=>c.urn===id) treated as a duplicate — selecting one 'selected all' via identity collision, and selectedConns effectively held a single conn. Fix: match by public_id (unique per connection). Verified: Select All now sets state to full connections array; UI shows '3 selected' and all 3 chips render. Bug 2 (Send fails): server-side LinkedIn API blocked from server IP. Fix: replace API send with clipboard copy + window.open(profile_url); verified clipboard content matches textarea and first profile URL opens.
